provenance_detail: Synthesized from: 14.4 desired state canon (workflow engine with approval gates, retries, checkpoints, branching; 8 core workflows; UBOS template library; workflow library screen; workflow run view screen), 14.6B onboarding spec (steps 12-14: generate workflows, SOPs, recurring tasks), 14.6B communication/delegation architecture (agent delegation to workflow steps, permission tier enforcement, approval protocol), projections/eos/workflows/ code truth (3 implemented workflows: OutreachWorkflow, FollowUpWorkflow, ContentCalendarWorkflow), 14.6B source detail preservation ledger (SIG-MOD-005, SIG-MOD-017, SIG-SCR-007, SIG-SCR-008, SIG-WF-001 through SIG-WF-008, SIG-FEAT-005, SIG-FEAT-017, SIG-FEAT-019), and operator corrections (hierarchy level 6: Workflows/SOPs/Tasks/Tools).
description: EOS Workflow and SOP Engine specification -- the complete model for how repeatable business processes are defined, stored, executed, governed, and optimized within EntrepreneurOS. Covers workflow/SOP data models, step types, execution modes, all 8 built-in workflows, UBOS template library, AI integration, governance gates, agent delegation, and task bridging.
design_principles: Workflows are the operational nervous system -- every repeatable business activity is a workflow, whether the operator knows it or not
Generate first, customize second -- onboarding produces workflows from entity type, stage, and complexity; operator refines
Three execution modes exist on a spectrum: fully manual, AI-assisted, and fully autonomous. The operator controls the dial per workflow, not per system
Every workflow step has a single owner (human role or AI agent) and a clear permission tier gate
Approval gates are governance, not friction -- they exist at risk boundaries, not at every step
SOPs are the knowledge layer beneath workflows -- a workflow defines WHAT happens, an SOP defines HOW each step is performed
Workflows evolve -- the self-improvement loop detects patterns, suggests refinements, and proposes new workflows from observed behavior

Deterministic spine first: trigger evaluation, step sequencing, state transitions, and timeout handling are all deterministic. AI enhances content generation, classification, and optimization within steps
Workflows are entity-scoped but template-shareable -- a workflow instance belongs to one entity, but the template can be reused across entities and even across operators via the UBOS library
Every workflow run produces a complete audit trail: who triggered it, what happened at each step, who approved what, what the outcome was, and how long it took

workflow_model.description: A Workflow is a defined sequence of steps that transforms inputs into outputs within a business operation. Workflows are the executable process layer in the EOS hierarchy (level 6: Workflows/SOPs/Tasks/Tools).

id.description: Unique identifier for the workflow definition

entity_id.description: The entity this workflow belongs to. Workflows are entity-scoped.

template_id.description: Reference to the template this workflow was instantiated from. Null if created from scratch.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier derived from name. Unique within entity.

description.description: Plain-text description of what this workflow accomplishes. Max 500 characters.

department.description: Primary department that owns this workflow. Null for cross-department workflows.

category.description: Functional category for grouping and filtering workflows in the library.

trigger.description: What starts a workflow run. Can be manual, scheduled, or event-driven.

type.description: manual = operator or agent explicitly starts it. scheduled = runs on a cron. event = triggered by a system event (new lead, payment received, etc.). signal = triggered by a UMH SignalEnvelope. condition = triggered when a KPI or metric crosses a threshold.

schedule.description: Cron expression for scheduled triggers. Null for non-scheduled.

schema.operator: enum (gt, lt, gte, lte, eq, crosses_above, crosses_below)

steps.description: Ordered list of steps in the workflow. See step_types for step schema.

execution_mode.description: Default execution mode. Can be overridden per-run. See execution_modes section.

risk_level.description: Risk classification of this workflow. Determines governance gates and approval requirements.

estimated_duration_minutes.description: Estimated time to complete one run of this workflow. Used for scheduling and capacity planning.

tags.description: Freeform tags for search and filtering.

linked_sops.description: SOP IDs that document how steps in this workflow should be executed.

linked_kpis.description: KPI IDs that this workflow contributes to or is measured by.

version.description: Monotonically increasing version number. Incremented on every structural edit.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the workflow definition.

created_by.description: User ID or agent ID that created this workflow.

states.description: Lifecycle states for a workflow definition (not a run).

draft.description: Newly created or under modification. Not executable.

active.description: Live and executable. Can be triggered manually, by schedule, or by event.

paused.description: Temporarily inactive. Existing runs can complete but new runs cannot start.

archived.description: Retired. Not executable. Preserved for audit and historical reference.

deprecated.description: Replaced by a newer version or workflow. Links to successor if applicable.

run_model.description: A WorkflowRun is a single execution instance of a workflow definition.

fields.trigger_context: object (event payload, manual parameters, or schedule metadata)
fields.execution_mode: enum (manual_stepthrough | hybrid_ai_assisted | fully_autonomous) -- may differ from workflow default
fields.status: enum (pending | running | paused | waiting_approval | completed | failed | cancelled | timed_out)
fields.outcome: object | null -- structured output of the completed workflow
fields.error: string | null -- error message if failed
fields.audit_trail: array<AuditEntry> -- every state change, approval, input, and output recorded

run_states.pending: Created but not yet started (e.g., queued for scheduled execution)
run_states.paused: Manually paused by operator or agent. Can be resumed.
run_states.waiting_approval: Blocked at an approval gate. Waiting for authorized approver.
run_states.completed: All steps finished successfully. Outcome recorded.
run_states.failed: A step failed and the workflow could not recover. Error recorded.
run_states.cancelled: Manually cancelled by operator or agent.
run_states.timed_out: Exceeded maximum allowed duration. Treated as failure.

branching.description: Workflows support conditional branching at any step. A step can define multiple branches with conditions, and the workflow engine evaluates them in order to determine the next step.

branch_types.conditional: If/else branching based on step output or workflow context. Evaluated deterministically.
branch_types.parallel: Multiple branches execute simultaneously. All must complete before the workflow continues (join).
branch_types.split: Multiple branches execute simultaneously. Workflow continues when ANY branch completes (race).
branch_types.loop: Repeat a sequence of steps until a condition is met or a maximum iteration count is reached.

branch_schema.condition: string (expression evaluated against step output and workflow context)
branch_schema.description: string (human-readable description of when this branch is taken)

sop_model.description: A Standard Operating Procedure is a documented, versioned, step-by-step instruction set for executing a specific task or group of tasks. SOPs are the knowledge layer -- they codify HOW things are done, while workflows codify WHAT happens. SOPs can be linked to workflow steps, roles, and departments.

entity_id.description: The entity this SOP belongs to.

examples: How to Qualify an Inbound Lead

purpose.description: Why this SOP exists -- what outcome it ensures. Max 300 characters.

scope.description: What activities and roles this SOP covers.

department.description: Owning department. Null for cross-department SOPs.

owner_role.description: The role responsible for maintaining and enforcing this SOP.

steps.description: Ordered list of instructions.

step_schema.tools_required: array<string> (tools or systems needed for this step)
step_schema.quality_criteria: string | null (how to verify this step was done correctly)

prerequisites.description: What must be true before this SOP can be executed.

exceptions.description: Known exceptions and how to handle them.

quality_criteria.description: How to verify the SOP was executed correctly as a whole.

linked_workflows.description: Workflow IDs that reference this SOP.

linked_roles.description: Roles that are expected to know and follow this SOP.

frequency.description: How often this SOP is typically executed.

schema.review_frequency: string (how often this SOP must be reviewed -- quarterly, annually, etc.)
schema.reviewed_by: string | null (user ID or role of last reviewer)
schema.compliance_score: number | null (0-100 based on execution adherence)
schema.deviations_logged: integer (count of logged deviations from this SOP)

version.description: Monotonically increasing. Incremented on every edit.

step_types.description: Every step in a workflow has a type that determines its execution behavior, UI representation, and governance requirements.

types.description: A step performed entirely by a human. The system tracks completion but does not execute anything. Operator or team member marks the step complete and optionally records output.
types.governance: No automatic approval needed -- the human performing it IS the executor

types.description: A step where AI generates a draft, recommendation, or analysis that a human reviews and optionally edits before proceeding. The AI output is a proposal, not an action.
types.ui: AI output panel with edit/approve/reject controls
types.governance: Human must explicitly approve AI output before the step is marked complete
examples: Draft outreach message (AI writes, human reviews)
Generate financial forecast (AI calculates, human validates)
Classify a support ticket (AI suggests category, human confirms)

types.description: A step executed entirely by an AI agent or system automation with no human in the loop. The step runs, records its output, and proceeds automatically. Used only for LOW risk actions within the agent's permission tier.
types.ui: Status indicator showing execution progress and outcome
types.governance: Must be within executing agent's permission tier. Risk level must be LOW. Audit trail recorded automatically.

types.description: A step that blocks workflow progress until an authorized approver grants approval. Used at risk boundaries: financial thresholds, legal actions, strategic decisions, external communications.
types.ui: Approval panel showing context, options (approve/reject/request_changes), and approver identity
types.governance: Requires explicit approval from a user or agent with sufficient permission tier. Configurable timeout with auto-escalation.

approval_schema.required_tier: enum (EXECUTE | COMMIT) -- minimum permission tier of approver
approval_schema.approvers: array<string> -- user IDs or role names authorized to approve
approval_schema.timeout_hours: integer | null -- auto-escalate if no response within this window
approval_schema.escalation_target: string | null -- who to escalate to on timeout
approval_schema.multi_approval: boolean -- whether multiple approvers are required (e.g., dual sign-off)
approval_schema.rejection_action: enum (halt | retry_previous | skip | branch) -- what happens on rejection

types.description: A step that evaluates a condition and records the result without blocking. Used for data validation, quality checks, and progress verification. If the check fails, the workflow can branch to a remediation path or flag the issue without halting.
types.governance: Checkpoint results are logged in the audit trail. Failures can trigger alerts or branches but do not inherently block.
examples: Check that all required fields are populated
Validate that KPI is within target range

types.description: A step that pauses the workflow until an external condition is met or a time duration elapses. Used for time-based delays, external event waits, and human response waits.
types.ui: Timer or condition indicator showing what the workflow is waiting for
types.governance: Maximum wait duration is configurable. Timeout behavior is configurable (proceed, fail, escalate).
examples: Wait 3 business days for client response

types.description: A step that sends a notification to one or more recipients without blocking the workflow. Used to inform stakeholders of progress, results, or required attention.
types.ui: Sent indicator with recipient list and message preview
types.governance: No approval needed. Audit trail records what was sent to whom.
examples: Alert finance team of large transaction

types.description: A step that triggers another workflow as a child run. The parent workflow can wait for the child to complete or continue in parallel. Used for composable, nested workflows.
types.ui: Link to child workflow run with status indicator
types.governance: Child workflow inherits parent's entity context. Child approval gates operate independently.
examples: Trigger employee onboarding workflow when hire is approved
Trigger compliance review workflow when contract is drafted

step_common_fields.step_id: string (unique within workflow, for branching references)
step_common_fields.name: string (human-readable step name)
step_common_fields.type: enum (manual | ai_assisted | fully_automated | approval_gate | checkpoint | wait | notification | subprocess)
step_common_fields.owner: string (role name or agent ID responsible for this step)
step_common_fields.timeout_minutes: integer | null (max time before step is considered stalled)
step_common_fields.on_failure: enum (halt | retry | skip | branch) -- behavior if step fails
step_common_fields.linked_sop_id: uuid | null -- SOP that documents how to perform this step
step_common_fields.metadata: object -- arbitrary key-value pairs for step-specific configuration

execution_modes.description: Three execution modes define the human-AI collaboration spectrum for running workflows. The operator sets the default mode per workflow and can override per run.

modes.description: The operator or assigned human steps through each workflow step manually. AI provides no automatic execution. The system tracks progress, shows the next step, and records outcomes -- but a human must explicitly advance each step. This is the most controlled mode.
when_to_use: New workflows being tested for the first time
Workflows where human judgment is required at every step
Operator wants maximum visibility and control
Training new team members on a process
modes.ai_role: AI is available on demand (operator can ask for help at any step) but takes no automatic action. AI may pre-populate fields or provide suggestions that the human can accept or ignore.
modes.approval_behavior: Approval gates present normally. All other steps also require human advancement.
modes.provenance: CODE_RESOLVED_CURRENT_TRUTH -- current projections/eos/workflows/ classes use this pattern (execute() returns result, no autonomous progression)

modes.description: AI agents execute automated steps and draft outputs for ai_assisted steps. Humans are pulled in for manual steps, approval gates, and review of AI-generated outputs. This is the default mode for most workflows -- it balances automation with human oversight.
when_to_use: Workflows with a mix of automated and judgment-requiring steps
Operator trusts AI for routine steps but wants to approve key outputs
modes.ai_role: AI executes fully_automated steps without human intervention. AI generates drafts for ai_assisted steps and presents them for human review. AI does not execute manual steps or bypass approval gates.
modes.approval_behavior: Approval gates block as designed. ai_assisted steps present AI output for human review. fully_automated steps execute silently with audit logging.
modes.provenance: SYNTHESIZED_CANON -- implied by the onboarding spec's hybrid agent-human execution model and the delegation architecture's permission tier system

modes.description: AI agents execute all steps without human intervention, including ai_assisted steps (AI approves its own drafts). Approval gates still block for COMMIT-tier actions. This mode requires explicit operator opt-in and is only available for LOW risk workflows or when the operator has configured high autonomy for the executing agent.
when_to_use: LOW risk, high-volume workflows that are well-tested
Scheduled workflows that run during off-hours
Operator has established trust in the workflow's reliability
modes.ai_role: AI executes all steps. For ai_assisted steps, AI generates and auto-approves output (recorded in audit trail as 'auto-approved by [agent]'). For manual steps, AI completes them if the step has an automated equivalent; otherwise the step is flagged for human attention.
modes.approval_behavior: Approval gates for COMMIT-tier actions still require human approval (this is a hard governance boundary). Approval gates for EXECUTE-tier and below can be auto-approved by the executing agent if operator has configured agent autonomy to allow it.
modes.provenance: SYNTHESIZED_CANON -- target state from 14.4 desired state ('execute workflows manually, hybrid, or autonomously') and the communication/delegation architecture's autonomy configuration in onboarding step 21
modes.governance_constraint: Fully autonomous mode requires: (1) workflow risk_level is LOW or operator has explicitly opted in for higher risk, (2) executing agent has sufficient permission tier for all steps, (3) operator has configured the agent's autonomy level to 'autonomous-within-bounds' or higher in agent configuration (onboarding step 21).

built_in_workflows.description: The 8 core workflows from the 14.4 desired state canon. These are the universal business workflows that EOS generates during onboarding (step 12) and makes available in the workflow library. Each workflow is described at the template level with full step breakdowns. Entity-type-aware generation customizes these templates based on the operator's business type, stage, and complexity.
built_in_workflows.source_reference: 14.4 desired state canon: workflows[] array (8 entries)

workflows.name: Business Setup
workflows.source_claim: Set up business operating system (create workspace, define company, get AI-generated org structure)
workflows.description: The foundational workflow that establishes a new entity's operational infrastructure. Executed primarily during onboarding (steps 8-19) but also available for adding new entities post-onboarding.

steps.name: Define Entity Identity
steps.description: Capture entity name, type, legal structure, and fundamental characteristics. AI suggests based on operator input.

steps.name: Select Business Stage
steps.description: Operator selects the current operational maturity stage (Idea through Enterprise).

steps.name: Define Goals and Constraints
steps.description: Capture strategic goals and operational constraints. AI suggests common goals/constraints for the entity type and stage.

steps.name: Select Complexity Level
steps.description: Operator selects operational complexity (Solo through Multi-Entity).

steps.name: Generate Organizational Structure
steps.description: AI generates org chart, departments, roles, and team structure based on entity type, stage, and complexity.

steps.name: Review and Approve Structure
steps.description: Operator reviews generated org chart, departments, and roles. Can edit before approving.

steps.name: Generate Operational Artifacts
steps.description: AI generates workflows, SOPs, recurring tasks, KPIs, and dashboard based on all prior context.

steps.name: Configure Agent Behavior
steps.description: Configure EA, CEO, and department agent behavior: autonomy level, communication style, focus areas.

steps.name: Set Approval Policies
steps.description: Configure governance: what requires approval, thresholds, and auto-approve rules.

steps.name: Final Review and Activation
steps.description: Operator reviews all generated artifacts and activates the entity workspace.

workflows.provenance_detail: Workflow from 14.4 desired state workflows[0]. Step breakdown synthesized from 14.6B onboarding spec (steps 4-25).

workflows.name: Daily Command Center Review
workflows.source_claim: See what matters today (home dashboard, KPIs, alerts, next-best actions, active workflows)
workflows.description: The daily operating rhythm. Surfaces what matters today: KPI status, alerts, priority tasks, active workflow runs, and AI-recommended next-best actions. This is the workflow behind the Home Dashboard.

steps.name: Aggregate Overnight Activity
steps.description: Collect all events, task completions, metric changes, and alerts since last review.

steps.name: Generate KPI Snapshot
steps.description: Pull current values for all tracked KPIs. Flag any that crossed thresholds.

steps.name: Generate Priority List
steps.description: AI ranks today's tasks and workflows by urgency and impact. Surfaces the top 5 priorities.

steps.name: Surface Next-Best Actions
steps.description: AI recommends 3-5 next-best actions based on goals, current pipeline, and detected opportunities/risks.

steps.name: Compile Morning Brief
steps.description: Assemble all above into the morning brief displayed on the Home Dashboard and delivered via EA.

steps.name: Deliver to Operator
steps.description: EA agent presents the morning brief to the operator via chat and dashboard.

workflows.provenance_detail: Workflow from 14.4 desired state workflows[1]. Step breakdown synthesized from CEO agent morning_brief skill, KPI dashboard generation (onboarding step 16), and communication architecture EA-to-operator briefing pattern.

workflows.name: Organizational Structure Management
workflows.description: The ongoing workflow for modifying the entity's organizational structure: adding departments, creating roles, adjusting responsibilities, and managing reporting lines. Initially set up during onboarding but evolves as the entity grows.

steps.name: Identify Structural Need
steps.description: Operator or CEO agent identifies a need for structural change (new department, new role, restructure).

steps.name: Analyze Impact
steps.description: AI analyzes the proposed change: affected workflows, reporting lines, permission scope, and budget impact.

steps.name: Generate Proposed Structure
steps.description: AI generates the proposed org chart change with role definitions, responsibilities, and permission tiers.

steps.name: Approve Structural Change
steps.description: Operator approves the proposed structural change.

steps.name: Apply Changes
steps.description: System applies the approved changes: creates/modifies departments, roles, permissions, and updates affected workflows.

steps.name: Update Affected Workflows
steps.description: System scans all workflows and SOPs for references to changed roles/departments and flags those needing updates.

steps.name: Notify Affected Parties
steps.description: Notify team members and agents affected by the structural change.

workflows.provenance_detail: Workflow from 14.4 desired state workflows[2]. Step breakdown synthesized from onboarding spec (steps 9-11), communication architecture (delegation protocol), and portfolio/entity ontology (Team, Agent, Role definitions).

workflows.name: Workflow/SOP Lifecycle
workflows.source_claim: Store and run workflows/SOPs (create or AI-generate, step through with AI)
workflows.description: The meta-workflow for creating, managing, and running workflows and SOPs. This is what powers the Workflow Library and Workflow Run View screens. Covers the full lifecycle from creation through execution through optimization.

steps.name: Identify Process Need
steps.description: Operator identifies a recurring process that should be formalized as a workflow or SOP.

steps.name: Draft Workflow/SOP
steps.description: AI generates a draft workflow or SOP based on the operator's description, entity type, and existing patterns. Operator reviews and edits.

steps.name: Define Steps and Owners
steps.description: AI suggests step sequence, step types, owners, and estimated durations. Operator refines.

steps.name: Set Governance Rules
steps.description: Operator configures approval gates, risk level, and execution mode for the new workflow.

steps.name: Test Run
steps.description: Execute the workflow in manual_stepthrough mode to validate the sequence and identify issues.

steps.name: Checkpoint: Test Run Successful
steps.description: Verify the test run completed without errors and produced expected outputs.

steps.name: Activate Workflow
steps.description: Operator approves the workflow for active use.

steps.name: Document as SOP
steps.description: AI generates a matching SOP document for the workflow, capturing step-by-step instructions and quality criteria.

workflows.provenance_detail: Workflow from 14.4 desired state workflows[3]. Step breakdown synthesized from Workflow Library screen spec, Workflow Run View screen spec, and SOP management design.

workflows.name: AI Planning and Drafting
workflows.source_claim: Use AI to plan and draft work (plans, documents, role definitions, workflow drafts, summaries)
workflows.description: The workflow for using AI to generate business artifacts: strategic plans, documents, role definitions, workflow drafts, meeting summaries, reports, and proposals. This powers the AI Copilot Workspace.

steps.name: Define Request
steps.description: Operator describes what they need: type of artifact, purpose, audience, constraints.

steps.name: Gather Context
steps.description: AI retrieves relevant context from entity memory: existing documents, KPIs, workflows, team structure, strategic goals.

steps.name: Generate Draft
steps.description: AI generates the requested artifact using entity context and the operator's specifications.

steps.name: Review and Refine
steps.description: Operator reviews the draft. Can request revisions, provide feedback, or edit directly. AI iterates.

steps.name: Finalize and Store
steps.description: Operator approves the final version. Document is stored in the entity's docs/notes workspace.

workflows.provenance_detail: Workflow from 14.4 desired state workflows[4]. Step breakdown synthesized from AI Copilot Workspace screen spec and Docs/Notes Workspace screen spec.

workflows.name: Task and Priority Management
workflows.source_claim: Track tasks and priorities (create/assign tasks, link to workflows, status dashboard)
workflows.description: The workflow for creating, assigning, tracking, and completing tasks. Tasks can be standalone or derived from workflow steps. This powers the Task Board/List screen.

steps.name: Create or Receive Task
steps.description: Task is created manually by operator, delegated by CEO agent, or generated from a workflow step.

steps.name: Classify and Prioritize
steps.description: AI classifies the task by domain, estimates effort, and suggests priority based on strategic alignment and deadlines.

steps.name: Assign to Owner
steps.description: Task is assigned to the appropriate role or agent based on department, skill match, and capacity.

steps.name: Execute Task
steps.description: The assigned owner (human or agent) performs the task and records output.

steps.name: Verify Completion
steps.description: System verifies that the task output meets quality criteria and all required fields are populated.

steps.name: Update Linked Workflows
steps.description: If the task was generated from a workflow step, update the parent workflow run's status.

workflows.provenance_detail: Workflow from 14.4 desired state workflows[5]. Step breakdown synthesized from Task Board/List screen spec and delegation architecture (CEO delegation protocol).

workflows.name: Business Context Persistence
workflows.source_claim: Keep business context persistent (memory stores company context, workflow context, preferences)
workflows.description: The background workflow that captures, stores, and retrieves business context. Every operator interaction, workflow run, decision, and metric change contributes to the entity's persistent memory. This powers the operating memory system and enables AI agents to have context-aware conversations.

steps.name: Detect Context Signal
steps.description: System detects a meaningful context change: operator decision, workflow outcome, KPI update, preference change, or new information from a conversation.

steps.name: Extract and Classify
steps.description: AI extracts structured facts, preferences, and decisions from the context signal. Classifies by type (fact, preference, decision, observation).

steps.name: Store in Memory
steps.description: Persist the extracted context to the entity's memory store with metadata (source, confidence, timestamp, expiry).

steps.name: Update Agent Context
steps.description: Propagate relevant context updates to agents that need them for their domains.

workflows.provenance_detail: Workflow from 14.4 desired state workflows[6]. Step breakdown synthesized from UMH memory system design and communication architecture (EA memory responsibilities).

workflows.name: KPI Review and Next-Best Actions
workflows.source_claim: Review key metrics and next-best actions (KPI cards, AI recommendations, portfolio views)
workflows.description: The periodic strategic review workflow. Provides deeper analysis than the daily command center: trend analysis, goal progress, competitive positioning, and strategic recommendations. Can be weekly, monthly, or quarterly depending on entity stage and operator preference.

steps.name: Compile KPI Data
steps.description: Pull KPI time-series data for the review period. Calculate trends, growth rates, and variance from targets.

steps.name: Analyze Trends
steps.description: AI analyzes KPI trends, identifies patterns, flags anomalies, and correlates metrics across departments.

steps.name: Assess Goal Progress
steps.description: AI evaluates progress toward strategic goals set during onboarding or last planning cycle. Flags at-risk goals.

steps.name: Generate Recommendations
steps.description: AI generates 3-5 strategic recommendations based on trend analysis, goal progress, and entity context.

steps.name: Compile Review Report
steps.description: Assemble findings into a structured review report with visualizations, trend charts, and recommendation cards.

steps.name: Present to Operator
steps.description: EA presents the review report to the operator with actionable next steps highlighted.

steps.name: Capture Operator Decisions
steps.description: Operator reviews recommendations, makes decisions, and the system captures them as strategic context for future workflows.

workflows.provenance_detail: Workflow from 14.4 desired state workflows[7]. Step breakdown synthesized from KPI dashboard generation (onboarding step 16), strategic context capture (onboarding step 6), and communication architecture (decision surfacing pattern).

template_library.description: The UBOS (Universal Business Operating System) Template Library provides franchise-like business templates that operators can instantiate for their entities. Templates include pre-configured workflows, SOPs, org charts, KPI sets, and agent configurations for specific business types.

ubos_templates.description: UBOS templates are curated, tested, complete business operating system templates. Each template is a full package that generates an entity's operational infrastructure when instantiated during onboarding or entity creation.

template_schema.name: string
template_schema.target_stage: array<string> (which stages this template is designed for)
template_schema.target_complexity: array<string> (which complexity levels this template supports)
template_schema.customization_points: array<string> (what the operator should customize after instantiation)
template_schema.author: string (creator or curator of the template)
template_schema.usage_count: integer (how many entities have been created from this template)

ubos_templates.mvp_scope: Initial templates for SaaS and Coaching/Info-Product (matching Initiate Arena and future product lines). Additional templates built progressively.
ubos_templates.end_state: Community-contributed template marketplace where operators can publish, rate, and fork templates.
ubos_templates.provenance_detail: UBOS template library from 14.4 desired state feature list (SIG-MOD-017, SIG-FEAT-017). Individual template breakdowns are INFERRED_PROFESSIONAL_GAP -- they do not exist in any prior source and are synthesized from professional knowledge of each business type's operational needs.

business_type_specific.description: Beyond UBOS templates, the workflow engine generates business-type-specific workflows dynamically during onboarding based on the operator's entity type selection (onboarding step 4). This is the entity-type-aware generation that serves as the MVP equivalent of the full template library.
business_type_specific.generation_logic: When an operator selects a business type, the generation engine selects from a matrix of workflows appropriate to that type. The 8 built-in workflows are always included; business-type-specific workflows are added on top.

saas.reasoning: SaaS businesses need product development cycles, subscription metrics tracking, and conversion optimization in addition to general business workflows.

agency.reasoning: Agencies need project-based delivery tracking, utilization management, and client relationship cycles beyond general sales and operations.

real_estate.reasoning: Real estate entities need property-specific operational workflows that do not exist in standard business operations.

investment.reasoning: Investment entities need portfolio management workflows focused on analysis, execution, and performance tracking rather than traditional sales/operations.

business_type_specific.provenance_detail: Synthesized from 14.6B onboarding spec step 12 (generate workflows based on entity_type, stage, departments, goals) and the 19 business types in the portfolio/entity ontology.

ai_integration.description: How AI is woven into the workflow engine at every level, from step execution to workflow generation to optimization.

step_level_ai.description: AI capabilities available at the individual step level.

capabilities.description: AI generates draft content for ai_assisted steps: messages, documents, reports, analyses, proposals. Human reviews before proceeding.
capabilities.deterministic_fallback: Template-based generation using entity context variables. Always produces usable output even if LLM is unavailable.
capabilities.current_code_truth: projections/eos/workflows/outreach.py _draft_message() implements this pattern: deterministic template first, AI enhancement when available.

capabilities.description: AI classifies inputs for routing, prioritization, and categorization at steps.
capabilities.deterministic_fallback: Rule-based classification using regex, keyword matching, and lookup tables.

capabilities.description: AI performs analytical tasks at steps: trend detection, anomaly identification, correlation analysis, sentiment analysis.
capabilities.deterministic_fallback: Statistical analysis (averages, standard deviations, threshold comparisons). AI adds pattern recognition and natural language insight.

capabilities.description: AI validates step outputs against quality criteria, checking for completeness, accuracy, and consistency.
examples: Validate that a contract covers all required clauses
Check that a report includes all requested metrics
capabilities.deterministic_fallback: Checklist-based validation: required fields present, value ranges correct, format valid.

capabilities.description: AI suggests the optimal next action based on workflow context, entity state, and historical patterns.
examples: Recommend which lead to contact next
capabilities.deterministic_fallback: Rules-based scoring (FIFO, priority, recency) to rank options.

workflow_generation.description: AI generates complete workflow definitions from operator descriptions, entity context, and business type knowledge.
generation_sources: Operator's natural language description of a process
Industry best practices (embedded in model knowledge)
workflow_generation.generation_output: Complete workflow definition including: name, steps with types and owners, trigger conditions, risk level, estimated duration, linked KPIs, and matching SOP draft.
workflow_generation.generation_trigger: Onboarding step 12 (generate workflows) and ongoing via AI Copilot ('create a workflow for...')
workflow_generation.provenance_detail: From 14.4 acceptance criteria: 'Founder can create or AI-generate workflows'. Generation capability synthesized from onboarding spec and AI Copilot Workspace design.

optimization.description: AI continuously monitors workflow performance and suggests optimizations.
optimization_signals: Frequent step failures at specific points
Underutilized or skipped steps (suggesting removal or simplification)
Repeated manual patterns that could be automated
Workflow runs that consistently deviate from the defined sequence
optimization_actions: Recommend automation of manual steps that show consistent patterns
Propose workflow consolidation when two workflows overlap significantly
Suggest new workflows when repeated ad-hoc patterns are detected
Recommend risk level adjustment based on historical execution data
optimization.provenance_detail: Self-improvement loop from 14.4 desired state (SIG-MOD-019, SIG-FEAT-019): 'pattern detection and workflow refinement'. Optimization mechanism synthesized from UMH feedback loop architecture.

governance.description: Governance mechanisms that ensure workflow execution is safe, auditable, and within authority boundaries.

approval_gates.description: Approval gates are governance checkpoints within workflows. They block progression until an authorized party approves the action.
placement_rules: Any step that involves financial transactions above a threshold
Any step that sends external communications to clients or prospects
Any step that modifies organizational structure (departments, roles, permissions)
Any step that creates legal obligations (contracts, commitments)
Any step that changes strategic parameters (KPI targets, goals, budgets)
Any step classified as HIGH or CRITICAL risk
Configurable: operator can add approval gates to any step via approval settings (onboarding step 22)

approval_flow.request: Executing agent or system queues an approval request with context, proposed action, and risk assessment
approval_flow.routing: Request routes to the authorized approver based on the step's required_tier and the entity's approval policies
approval_flow.decision: Approver reviews and chooses: approve, reject, or request_changes
approval_flow.approve: Workflow proceeds to the next step. Approval recorded in audit trail.
approval_flow.reject: Workflow takes the rejection_action path: halt, retry_previous, skip, or branch to remediation
approval_flow.request_changes: Workflow returns to the previous step with the approver's feedback for revision
approval_flow.timeout: If no decision within timeout_hours, request escalates to the escalation_target. If no escalation target, the workflow enters waiting_approval state indefinitely until resolved.

approval_gates.provenance_detail: 14.4 desired state: 'Workflow engine with approval gates'. Approval flow synthesized from 14.6B communication architecture approval protocol and onboarding step 22 (configure approval settings).

risk_classification.description: Every workflow and every step is classified by risk level. Risk classification determines governance requirements.

LOW.governance: No approval gate required. Audit trail recorded. Fully autonomous execution allowed.

MEDIUM.description: Actions with moderate business impact or limited reversibility.
MEDIUM.governance: Approval gate recommended but not required. AI-assisted mode recommended. Audit trail recorded.

HIGH.description: Actions with significant business impact or difficult reversibility.
HIGH.governance: Approval gate required. Manual or hybrid mode required. Cannot run fully autonomous. Audit trail with full context.

CRITICAL.description: Actions with severe, potentially irreversible business impact.
CRITICAL.governance: Dual approval gate required (two authorized approvers). Manual stepthrough mode required. CEO agent involvement mandatory. Complete audit trail with operator sign-off.

audit_trail.description: Every workflow run produces a complete, immutable audit trail.
recorded_events: Run created (who triggered, why, what context)
Each step failed (timestamp, error, retry count)
Workflow state transitions (running, paused, waiting_approval, etc.)
AI-generated content (what was generated, what was approved, what was modified by human)
Escalation events (who escalated to whom, why)
Manual overrides (operator bypassed a step or changed execution mode mid-run)
audit_trail.storage: Audit entries persist to Neon Postgres with RLS scoped by entity_id. Queryable through the activity feed and workflow run detail view.
audit_trail.retention: Audit trails are never deleted. Archived workflow runs retain their complete audit trail.

agent_delegation.description: How EOS agents interact with workflows: which agents execute which steps, how delegation works, and how escalation flows.

delegation_model.description: Agent delegation to workflow steps follows the communication/delegation architecture. The CEO agent is the primary workflow orchestrator within an entity.

ceo_agent.role_in_workflows: Primary orchestrator. Receives workflow triggers (from EA or scheduler), selects which department agent should execute each step, monitors progress, and handles cross-department coordination.
ceo_agent.delegates_to: Department agents based on step domain and required skills

ea_agent.role_in_workflows: Communication layer. Delivers workflow outputs to operator, surfaces approval requests, and captures operator decisions. Does NOT execute domain steps.
ea_agent.delegates_to: Never -- EA routes to CEO or Portfolio Advisor, not to department agents

department_agents.role_in_workflows: Domain executors. Each department agent executes steps within its domain.

escalation.description: Escalation within workflows follows the delegation architecture's escalation protocol.
escalation.within_workflow: If a department agent cannot complete a step (insufficient permission, ambiguity, cross-department dependency), it escalates to the CEO agent who either resolves the issue or escalates further to the EA for operator input.
escalation.to_operator: Escalation to operator always flows through the EA agent. The EA formats the escalation as a decision with context, options, and recommendation.

task_integration.description: How workflows and tasks interoperate. Workflows generate tasks, tasks can trigger workflows, and both share a unified tracking surface.

workflow_to_task_bridge.description: Workflow steps can generate tasks that are tracked independently in the task management system.
generation_rules: When a workflow step is assigned to a human role, a task is automatically created in the task board with a link back to the workflow run
Recurring workflows generate recurring tasks at each scheduled run
Subprocess steps generate child tasks in the parent task's context
Approval gate steps generate approval tasks in the approver's task queue

task_fields_from_workflow.title: Derived from step name
task_fields_from_workflow.priority: Derived from workflow risk_level and step position
task_fields_from_workflow.due_date: Derived from workflow schedule and step estimated_duration

status_sync.description: Task status and workflow step status are kept in sync bidirectionally.
status_sync.task_to_workflow: When a task is marked complete, the corresponding workflow step is marked complete and the workflow advances.
status_sync.workflow_to_task: When a workflow run is cancelled or fails, all pending tasks generated from that run are cancelled with a reference to the workflow event.
status_sync.conflict_resolution: If a task is completed but the workflow step checkpoint fails validation, the task is reopened with the failure reason.

current_code_truth.description: Ground truth from projections/eos/workflows/ as of 2026-06-04

implemented_workflows.execution_mode: manual_stepthrough (execute() returns result, no autonomous progression)
implemented_workflows.ai_integration: AI-enhanced draft generation via call_with_fallback with deterministic template fallback
implemented_workflows.instance_specific_concern: outreach.py references 'Initiate Arena' in AI prompt system message. Needs generalization.

implemented_workflows.trigger: Lead has not responded in N days
implemented_workflows.ai_integration: Purely deterministic (template-based follow-up messages by staleness tier). No AI call.
AI-enhanced content ideation via call_with_fallback with deterministic template fallback
implemented_workflows.instance_specific_concern: content.py references 'Lyfe Institute / Initiate Arena' in AI prompt. Needs generalization.

not_implemented: Workflow definition data model (workflows are Python classes, not DB-persisted definitions)
Workflow run tracking (no run model, no state machine, no audit trail)
SOP model (no SOP data structure exists)
Approval gates (steps return 'pending_approval' status but no approval mechanism exists)
Workflow run view UI (no step-through execution UI)
Trigger system (no scheduled, event, or condition triggers)
AI optimization loop (no workflow performance monitoring)
current_code_truth.architectural_assessment: Current implementation is a valid pattern for the workflow execution engine (Python classes with step methods, deterministic spine with AI enhancement). The gap is the infrastructure layer: data model persistence, run tracking, trigger system, governance gates, and UI surfaces. The existing code can serve as the execution backend; the data model and orchestration layer must be built on top.

r3_scope.description: R3 (Workflows) is the third MVP release. It delivers the workflow library, workflow runner, and AI-assisted workflow drafting.
included: Workflow definition data model persisted in Neon Postgres
Workflow library screen: browse, search, filter active workflows
Workflow creation: manual definition and AI-generated from description
Workflow run view: step-through execution with manual and hybrid modes
Basic step types: manual, ai_assisted, approval_gate, checkpoint
Basic approval gates with single-approver flow
SOP creation and linking to workflow steps
3 pre-built workflows matching current code (outreach, follow-up, content)
8 built-in workflow templates generated during onboarding
not_included_in_r3: Fully autonomous execution mode (requires mature agent configuration from R4)
Event-driven and condition-based triggers (requires event bus infrastructure)
Branching beyond simple conditional (parallel, split, loop)
Workflow optimization AI (requires historical run data)
Subprocess step type (requires recursive workflow runs)

to_r4: AI Copilot integration for natural language workflow creation
Agent autonomy configuration affecting workflow execution mode
Fully autonomous mode with governed boundaries
to_r5_plus: Workflow optimization AI with pattern detection
Workflow versioning with diff and rollback
end_state_only: Skill marketplace integration (workflows can be packaged as skills)
Self-improving workflows (system autonomously refines based on patterns)
Enterprise-grade compliance workflows with regulatory templates

open_questions.question: Should workflow definitions be version-controlled with full diff history, or is a simple version number with snapshots sufficient for MVP?
open_questions.default_assumption: Simple version number with snapshots for MVP. Full diff history is end-state.

open_questions.question: Should the UBOS template library be curated-only (EOS team publishes templates) or community-contributed from the start?
open_questions.default_assumption: Curated-only for MVP and early releases. Community contribution is end-state. This aligns with 14.4 open question about UBOS community vs curated.
open_questions.prior_reference: SIG-OQ-004 in source detail preservation ledger

open_questions.question: Should workflows support real-time collaboration (multiple operators step through the same run simultaneously) or is single-operator execution sufficient?
open_questions.default_assumption: Single-operator execution for MVP. Real-time collaboration is end-state for multi-team entities.

open_questions.question: How should the workflow engine handle long-running steps (days or weeks)? Should there be a maximum step duration or do steps persist indefinitely until completed?
open_questions.default_assumption: Steps persist indefinitely with configurable reminders and escalation timeouts. No hard maximum. Stale step detection surfaces warnings after configurable thale period.

open_questions.question: Should the operator be able to modify a workflow definition while a run is in progress? If so, does the running instance use the old definition or switch to the new one?
open_questions.default_assumption: Running instances use the definition version that was active when the run started. New runs use the updated definition. This is standard workflow engine behavior.

open_questions.question: For the 8 built-in workflows, should all 8 be generated for every entity type during onboarding, or should entity-type filtering exclude irrelevant ones (e.g., 'Business Context Persistence' is universal but 'Org Structure Management' may be skipped for solo operators)?
open_questions.default_assumption: All 8 are generated for every entity. For solo operators, steps involving team/department management are simplified or marked as 'activate when you scale'. No workflow is hidden -- the operator sees the full potential of their operating system.

open_questions.question: Should SOP compliance tracking be automatic (system detects when a workflow run deviates from its linked SOP) or manual (operator marks compliance)?
open_questions.default_assumption: Automatic detection for measurable deviations (step order, step skipping, duration thresholds). Manual for qualitative compliance. Hybrid approach.

open_questions.question: How should financial approval thresholds work across entities within a portfolio? Per-entity thresholds, portfolio-level thresholds, or both?
open_questions.default_assumption: Per-entity thresholds with optional portfolio-level overrides. Entity CEO agent enforces entity thresholds; Portfolio Advisor flags portfolio-level concerns.

implementation_debt.description: Workflow definitions are Python classes (projections/eos/workflows/), not persisted data models. Must build data model in Neon with Drizzle ORM schema to enable dynamic creation, editing, and template instantiation.
No workflow run tracking or state machine exists. Must build WorkflowRun model with state transitions, step results, and audit trail.
Approval gates return 'pending_approval' status but no approval mechanism, queue, or resolution flow exists. Must build approval request/response system tied to permission tiers.
No trigger system exists. Workflows can only be executed by direct Python method call. Must build trigger infrastructure for scheduled, event-driven, and condition-based triggers.
Instance-specific references in outreach.py ('Initiate Arena') and content.py ('Lyfe Institute / Initiate Arena'). Must be generalized to use entity context from BIS runtime lookup.
No SOP data model or storage exists. Must build SOP model with versioning, compliance tracking, and linking to workflow steps.
No Workflow Library or Workflow Run View UI exists in the SaaS layer. Must build both screens as defined in 14.4 desired state screens list.
No UBOS template system exists. Must build template schema, storage, instantiation logic, and (for end-state) marketplace infrastructure.
